headline: DPSC Limited: Bank Guarantee Invocation Triggers Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process
sum: DPSC Limited has intimated the stock exchange of a bank guarantee invocation that triggered entry into CIRP. The notification under Regulation 30 of SEBI LODR indicates formal insolvency proceedings have commenced.
implication: Bank guarantees in corporate debt structures now constitute a material disclosure trigger for listed companies; invocation accelerates CIRP filing and creates immediate reporting obligations to exchanges.
detail: DPSC Limited has informed NSE of the invocation of a bank guarantee, which serves as a creditor action precipitating admission into the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process. The company's disclosure under Regulation 30 of the SEBI Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements indicates that a financial covenant or payment default has been crystallised, and a secured creditor has called upon the guarantee. This intimation is the mandatory first public signal of insolvency proceedings.

framework.ref: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, Part II (CIRP) - Sections 7–29
framework.note: central - statutory framework governing admission, resolution, and claims in corporate insolvency; bank guarantee invocation is a common trigger for creditor petition under s.7.
central - mandatory requirement for listed companies to disclose material events; CIRP and guarantee invocation qualify as material corporate events.

framework.ref: IBBI (Insolvency Resolution Process for Corporate Persons) Regulations, 2016
framework.note: central - procedural rules governing IP appointment, process timelines (180 + 90 days), resolution plan evaluation.

framework.ref: NCLT (National Company Law Tribunal) Rules, 2016, Part B
framework.note: central - jurisdiction, admission process, and bench procedures for CIRP cases.
amended - governs NSE's power to enforce listing rules and require immediate disclosure of material events.
peripheral - bank guarantee is a contract of suretyship; invocation triggers creditor's legal rights under ICA.

conditions: Bank guarantee invoked by secured creditor
Company unable or unwilling to discharge underlying obligation
approvals: NCLT admission order (pending; not yet public)
structure.novel: Regulation 30 intimation of guarantee invocation as a distinct material event, distinct from conventional default announcement.

triggers.note: guarantee invocation by secured creditor typically triggers creditor-initiated CIRP petition to NCLT.
listed company must disclose CIRP admission and material contractual events (guarantee calls) within 30 minutes of stock exchange opening or as soon as practicable.
NCLT admission order must be passed within 14 days of creditor petition filing; thereafter, IP takes charge and issues public notice.
